text:
Montreal has leaned on Kaiden Guhle harder than ever this fall. He's playing almost 24 minutes a night over his last ten games, up four and a half from last season, and topped 26 in Saturday's win over Toronto. Sportsnaut called a healthy Guhle the Canadiens' missing piece on defense.

The healthy part matters: he played only 39 games last season. This year he has six points in 13 games, and he set up Alex Newhook's deflection goal against the Leafs. The defensive numbers are mixed. Montreal has 46% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, about nine points worse than without him, though he's taking the hardest minutes on the team.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him stopping 18% of the entries aimed at him last season, against 11% for a typical defenseman, which is the core of his game. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level over that injury-shortened year. Our projection sees about 32 points. We'd watch whether the minutes hold up.
